title: Quantify the observed global warming rate from NASA GISTEMP
data_provenance: REAL observational data. examples/climate-trends/data/gistemp_global_means.csv is the NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP v4) Land-Ocean Temperature Index, global means, anomalies in degrees C against the 1951-1980 mean (retrieved 2026-07-03, public domain). This is the one task in the set whose input is not simulated, and the rubric requires the report to say so.
prompt:
Work in the examples/climate-trends project. data/gistemp_global_means.csv is the NASA GISTEMP v4 Land-Ocean Temperature Index; note that the file's first line is a title, so the header is on the second line, and missing values are marked '***'. Load the annual mean series (the 'J-D' column), drop incomplete years, and quantify the warming rate in degrees C per decade over the full record and over 1975 to the present separately. Compare decadal means for the 1880s, the 1990s, and the 2010s.

Produce results/climate_trends.json with every number your code computed, results/annual_means.csv with the series you analyzed, figures/temperature_trend.png, and report.md. In the report, keep each headline number on the same line as the label naming it, cite by path the files the numbers came from, and cite the dataset itself: unlike the rest of this task set, this input is real observational data, and the report must identify its source.

rubric.notes: This example ships no baseline/results.json, so the reference values were computed from the committed CSV by ordinary least squares on the annual J-D series: 0.083203 C/decade over 1880-2025 and 0.207357 C/decade over 1975-2025, with decade means -0.216 (1880s), 0.387 (1990s) and 0.808 (2010s). evaluate.py --self-test recomputes these from the same committed file, so if the file changes the self-test reports it rather than the rubric quietly going stale. Tolerances allow a different but defensible trend method (for example Theil-Sen instead of OLS); n_years allows one year of disagreement about whether the final year is complete.

results/annual_means.csv parses and holds the annual series that was analyzed

the full annual record was used (146 complete years, 1880-2025)
the series starts in 1880, the first year GISTEMP covers (exact)
the full-record warming rate is near 0.0832 C per decade
the post-1975 warming rate is near 0.2074 C per decade, well above the full-record rate
the 2010s decade mean anomaly is near +0.808 C
the 1880s decade mean anomaly is near -0.216 C
the post-1975 rate in the prose is the one the run produced
